digest.component_or_area: Jira DC bidirectional reconciler live verification
propositions: Epic e369's headline acceptance criterion — bidirectional reconciliation against the Dockerized Jira instance with data actually moving in both directions — is not met, because the passing CI run converged only against an empty harness instance where scanned=0 proves nothing.

The live verification must run against a scrubbed copy of the real ticket store, obtained by explicitly fetching the gitignored orphan 'tickets' branch and extracting into .tickets-tracker/, with a written rebar.toml pointing only at the harness.

Isolation must be enforced by a fresh git repo with no remotes and REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off, asserted by tests that fail the job if 'git remote' returns anything, so auto-push cannot leak test mutations to the real project.

The copy must be scrubbed of all .bridge_state* artifacts (bindings, retired bindings, prev_snapshot, including the .bak-retarget backup) matched by glob and asserted absent by enumerating the tree, since surviving bindings hold real production Jira keys.

A comprehensive suite of fourteen inbound and fourteen outbound DC mutations must each round-trip and be asserted individually against a named per-mutation oracle, except set_parent's epic case which is asserted directly against the transport with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError).

Pagination is a remote-side property not exercised by the store copy, so the suite must observe the server's effective page size, seed at least 2*observed+1 harness issues, poll the search index until settled, and assert full recovery via the dry-run plan.
